newsitem.title: USA: Deloitte & Touche LLP to pay civil penalty to CFTC.
newsitem.headline: Deloitte & Touche LLP to pay civil penalty to CFTC.

text.p: Deloitte & Touche LLP, one of the largest U.S. accounting firms, agreed to pay a $100,000 civil penalty to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission after the CFTC filed a complaint against the firm and its former partner Thomas Lux, the CFTC said.
The CFTC said this was the first time it had censured an individual auditor for unprofessional conduct and the complaint was the third filed against a major accounting firm.
The CFTC's complaint said Lux failed to audit First Commercial Financial Group Inc's 1993-94 financial statements in accordance with generally accepted auditing standards(GAAS).
The CFTC also said in its complaint that Lux failed to properly investigate and report on material inadequacies in First Commercial's internal controls.
The complaint said Lux was made aware of material inadequacies during the audit, but had concluded in his report to the CFTC that there were no material inadequacies.

"These professionals play a vital role in maintaining the integrity of our futures markets and often provide the public with its first line of defense against undercapitalized or unscrupulous entities," Geoffrey Aronow, CFTC enforcement director, said in a statement.

The CFTC said Lux failed to make appropriate inquiries under GAAS when he found First Commercial made disbursements in the form of unsecured loans in excess of $1.6 million, and did not disclose the effect of the unsecured loans on First Commercial's capitalization.
First Commercial, which was a Chicago-based futures commission merchant, was forced by the CFTC to close down in December 1994.
The CFTC later filed a complaint against the firm and two of its principals for operating while undercapitalized and filing "willfully false" statements with the CFTC.

Deloitte & Touche said in a statement that the CFTC's order found no firmwide or systematic problems with respect to Deloitte's auditing processes and procedures, and that no customers of First Commercial experienced losses as a result of the audit at issue.
